title: HMAC: HmacCtx struct leaked after every wc_HmacFinal — crypto2dev_free_hmac is dead code
description: Root cause: wc_HmacFree() does NOT call wc_CryptoCb_Free(WC_ALGO_TYPE_FREE, WC_ALGO_TYPE_HMAC) — confirmed by grepping wolfcrypt/src/hmac.c: there is no wc_CryptoCb_Free call anywhere in the file. Instead, wolfSSL's cleanup convention for HMAC devCtx is the wc_CryptoCb_Hmac(hmac, macType, NULL, 0, finalHash) call in wc_HmacFree (line 1441 of hmac.c), where digest=finalHash is the signal to treat this as Final+cleanup. Consequence: crypto2dev_free_hmac() (crypto2dev_port.c, the WC_ALGO_TYPE_FREE/HMAC path) is NEVER invoked — it is unreachable dead code. The HmacCtx struct (including key bytes) allocated by HMAC SETKEY is NEVER freed, because our crypto2dev_hmac() Final path only frees ctx->data but not the ctx struct itself and does not NULL hmac->devCtx. Every wc_HmacFinal()+wc_HmacFree() cycle leaks sizeof(Crypto2DevHmacCtx) bytes of heap-allocated key material. A TLS server doing one HMAC per record leaks one context struct per record. Fix: in crypto2dev_hmac() Final path, after freeing ctx->data, also ForceZero+XFREE the ctx struct and set hmac->devCtx = NULL. This also stops the spurious extra HMAC computation that wc_HmacFree triggers (because devCtx == NULL, wc_HmacFree skips the callback). crypto2dev_free_hmac() can remain as a safety net.
